name: Pipeline widget
summary: A widget that shows the pipeline engine at a glance: a row of status squares, one per plugin, with the detail on hover, the status line beside them, what is running now and the queue, and a chart of recent runs (name, area, run time, how long ago, runs).
description: The pipeline widget came back 2026-10-12 on the owner's request ("yes bring them back", #1689) after the other operator's #1682 U1 removed the old job version. It is global only, off the surface until you place it, and it draws the new engine. On top is a row of status squares (item 519), one per plugin the engine runs (stats, deep search, and any later one), each showing its state by shape as well as color the way the old job widget did: a filled green circle caught up, a yellow ring behind, a coral diamond failing, a gray dash when the engine is off; a rebuild shows as behind and says rebuilding. Hovering a square, focusing it with the keyboard or tapping it opens its detail: how many files wait and how old the oldest is, when it last delivered, its last error and how many are failing, and how many runs since the server started. The squares carry no rebuild button (2026-10-12): a rebuild is done from Settings, pipeline. The overall status line (caught up, behind, stalled, rebuilding or off) sits small beside the row. Under it are two short sections (2026-10-12): running lists each plugin on the transcript being delivered right now (and any rebuild in progress) with its area and how long it has run, ticking in the browser; queue lists the next transcripts waiting in the order the engine takes them, at most eight and then "+N more", each for all plugins or the one plugin whose retry holds it, with its area (a live transcript whose session name is not known yet shows its short id) and how long it has waited, or when its retry is due. The engine announces a delivery when it starts as well as when the batch ends, so running shows without polling. Under those is the pipeline chart (item 542, #1701): one row per area and plugin, updated in place rather than a row per run, with the plugin's friendly name, its area (the session's name, else the project's, else machine for work with no session such as a catch-up scan of an old conversation or a rebuild), how long the last run took, how long ago that was (ticking in the browser with no request) and how many runs since the server started. A failed run wears a diamond mark, a parked one a dash. Every figure column keeps the room its widest value needs, so the run time is never cut off; the name and area give way first, and a very narrow widget drops the runs and then the area before any figure. The server keeps these rows in memory only (about 100, empty after a restart); it records and logs, it never alerts. Every view shares one read of GET /api/v1/pipeline/status, pushed on the pipeline topic after every batch, park, scan pass and rebuild, so nothing polls while the live connection is up (a 10 second poll runs only while it is down). The developer widget carries it as its pipeline tab. While the conversation backups plugin is on, the chart also shows a backups row (area conversations, #1807): its 30 minute passes plus the captures on close, sleep, restart, clear and fork as runs, the last run's time and duration, and a failed mark when the latest pass or capture failed; with the plugin off the row is not there. It comes through a plugin seam (src/cplugs/sdk/pipeline_rows.py), so the plugin stays self contained.
where: Home screen once added: a cell titled pipeline with a database mark.
The drawer's widget area, once added.
how_to: Open the edit layout control at the bottom of the drawer.
Search widgets for pipeline; press the card to put it on the home page, or press the one under drawer area to put it in the drawer.
Read the status squares and the line beside them, then the chart below: one row per session (or project, or machine) and plugin.
Read running for what the engine is delivering now and queue for what waits next.
Hover or focus a square to see its backlog, last delivery, last error and runs.
To rebuild a plugin, open Settings, pipeline and press rebuild beside it.
examples: See at a glance which plugin is behind or failing by the shape of its square.
See at once whether deep search is behind and by how many files.
See which session the stats plugin last read, how long it took and how long ago.
See that eleven transcripts wait after a restart, and which plugin a failing one waits on.
media_exempt: A widget whose screenshots are captured before the next version bump.
